sentences.text: This claim petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioner is as follows:-
That on 05.09.2024 at about 1.00 to 1.10 p.m., the petitioner along with two others was traveling in the Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-03-EG-1766-7909 as pillion rider to have food towards ISRO Layout, on the left side of the road.

When they reached near Aksha Vihara Layout junction, at that time the driver of the School Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-50-A-2110 by driving his vehicle in a rash and negligent manner dashed to the petitioner's motor cycle, result of which the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately, the petitioner was shifted to Yelahanka Govt. Hospital, wherein first aid treatment was given and then he was shifted to Prolife Multispeciality Hospital wherein admitted as an inpatient.
So far, the petitioner has spend more than sum of Rs.2,50,000/- towards medial expenses and incidental charges.
The petitioner has to undergo future treatment and physiotherapy at the cost of Rs.1,00,000/-.
3. Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy.
He was aged about 18 years.
He was working with his uncle and earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
Due to the permanent disability, he is not in a position to do the said work.
He has suffered pain and sufferings, permanent disability and loss of income.

4. The respondent No.1/ the R.C. owner of School Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-50-A-2110 has filed written statement and contended that at the time of accident, petitioner was not at all traveling in the motorcycle and that there was three person traveling in the motorcycle and all of them were minors and the petitioner is falsely claiming that he was also traveling in the motorcycle in order to claim the compensation.

It is further contended that the driver of the School bus was holding valid and effective driving licence and that on the stated date, after dropping the kids at Ganteganahalli village, the Van was heading towards Singanayakanahalli village to drop other kids, on that way Syed was with two others in the motorcycle and the rider of the motorcycle by riding the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner dashed to the school bus.
6. Respondent no.2/

the insurer of School Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-50-A-2110 has filed written statement and contended that the driver of the School Bus was not holding valid and effective driving license and the said vehicle was not having valid RC, Permit and Fitness certificate and that after thorough investigation, they have charge sheeted both the driver of the bus and the rider of the motorcycle in which petitioner was traveling as pillion rider and rider of the motorcycle was charge sheeted as accused no.2 u/Sec. 128 of MV Act for triple riding.

The respondent no.2 further Nikhil M vs Seshadripuram Public School on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140074050/
2 contended that as per the rough sketch and the spot mahazar, the bus has crossed almost 80% of the cross road, at that time the rider of the motorcycle without observing the bus negligently rode the motorcycle and dashed to the bus.

sentences.text:
7. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that he had sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident on 05-09-2024 at about 1.00 to 1.10 p.m., ISRO Layout, Near Aksha Vihara Layout, Yelahanka, Bengaluru due to rash and negligence driving of the driver of School Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-50-A-2110?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
3.

What Order or Award?
8.
The petitioner got examined himself as Pw1 and examined three witnesses as P.W.1 to P.W.3 and marked Ex.P1 to Ex.P20.
The respondents have not led evidence on their side.

9. Heard arguments of learned counsel for the petitioner and respondents and perused the entire materials placed on record.
10.

My findings on the above issues are as follows:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly in the affirmative.

Issue No.3: As per final order, for the following;
REASONS 11. Issue No.1 : - In order to explain the actionable negligence of the driver of School Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-50-A-2110, the P.W.1 has filed his affidavit explaining the vivid picture of the accident that took place on 05.09.2024 at about 1.00 to 1.10 p.m., when the petitioner along with two others was traveling in the Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-03-EG-1766-7909 as pillion rider to have food towards ISRO Layout, on the left side of the road.

When they reached near Aksha Vihara Layout junction, at that time the driver of the School Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-50-A-2110 (herein after called the offending vehicle) by driving his vehicle in a rash and negligent manner dashed to the petitioner's motor cycle, result of which he fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

P.W.1 further deposed about the nature of injuries sustained, treatment taken and the amount spent for treatment etc.
12.

In support of the claim and to prove the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle, the P.W.1 has relied upon Ex.P1 to 7 which are the police records such as FIR with complaint, crime Nikhil M vs Seshadripuram Public School on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140074050/
3 details, sketch, IMV reports, wound certificate, charge sheet, Notice Under Se.133 of IMV Report etc.,
13.

sentences.text: On the basis of the complaint lodged by the petitioner, case has been registered against the driver of the offending vehicle in Crime No.286/2024 of Yelahanka Traffic PS., for the offence punishable under section 125 (b) & 281 of BNS Act.

The investigation officer after investigation has filed charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle as accused no.1 and the rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-03-EG-1766 as accused no.2 for the offence punishable under section 128 of IMV Act.
14.
The petitioner who got examined as PW.1 in his cross examination has admitted that at the time of accident three persons were traveling in the motorcycle.
Though the respondent no.1 has taken the contention that the rider of the motorcycle was minor but no evidence to that effect has been placed.
The respondent no.1 has taken the further defence that the petitioner was not at all traveling in the aforesaid motorcycle.

But if the police intimation and MLC produced by the petitioner is perused, soon after the accident the petitioner has taken treatment at Government Hospital Yelahanka and thereafter he was shifted to Prolife Multi Specialty Hospital.
In the MLC and police intimation, history of the accident is mentioned as "Two wheeler hit by bus".
Further respondent no.1 has not adduced evidence of their driver to say that the petitioner was not in the motorcycle at the time of accident.
Hence, there is every reason to believe that petitioner was traveling in the motorcycle and he sustained injuries due to the accident.

15. So far as the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is concerned, if the spot mahazar and sketch is perused, at the time of accident the offending vehicle was proceeding from Aksha Vihara Layout road towards ISRO Layout.
The motorcycle of the petitioner was proceeding from Aksha Vihara Layout which exist towards the left side of the road.
The motorcycle by coming from the left side of the road has already entered the main road.
The offending vehicle which was coming some where in the middle of the road when it reached to the spot of the accident took the vehicle towards left side and hit to the motorcycle.
Hence, the spot mahazar and sketch clearly discloses the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle.
It is true that there was triple riding in the motorcycle.
But for the violation of the traffic rules, the rider of the motorcycle was prosecuted.
Hence, the mere fact that there was triple riding in the motorcycle, no amount of negligence can be fastened on the rider of the motorcycle.
Hence, without discussing much on this point this court holds issue no.1 in the affirmative.
16. Issue No.2:- The petitioner has given evidence to the effect of his sustained grievous injuries.
As observed earlier, petitioner has produced medical documents i.e., Wound certificate, Discharge summary and Inpatient Bill which are at Ex.P5, Ex.P8 and Ex.P10.

On going through the medical documents, it reveals that petitioner has taken treatment at Prolife Multi Specialty Hospital wherein admitted as an inpatient from 05-09-2024 to 10-09-2024 for a period of 6 days.
As per the wound certificate, the petitioner has sustained two injuries of which one is simple in nature and another is grievous in nature.

Lakshmi T N -Medical Record Officer at Prolife Hospital, Bengaluru is examined as PW.2 and through him police intimation, MLC, case sheet and x-ray films are got marked as Ex.P15 and Ex.P18.
18.
Dr. S.A.Somashekara, the Orthopaedic Surgeon at Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru is examined as Pw3 and through him X-ray and OPD are got marked as Ex.P.19 and Ex.P20.
P.W.3 has deposed that he examined the petitioner on 29-09-2025 clinically, radiologically for disability assessment.

PW.3 further deposed that petitioner has sustained permanent physical disability of right lower limb at 36% and whole body disability at 18% and that petitioner needs surgery for removal of implant which would cost around Rs.40,000/- in private set up.
19. If the cross examination of PW.3 is carefully perused, PW.3 is not a treated doctor.
As per the own evidence of the PW.3, the fracture is united.
The petitioner is aged about 18 years.
20. Though PW.3 has assessed the disability of petitioner on right lower limb at 36% but he has assessed the disability on whole body at 18%.

As per the judgment reported in 2014 (4) Kar.L.J 157 Vijaya Kumar Alias Babu Rao Vs The Secretary, Agricultural Produce Marketing Committee Balki,
Taluk the normal rule would be disability in the lower limb would be 1/3 rd of the particular limb.

entities.text:
2014 (4) Kar.L.J 157 Vijaya Kumar Alias Babu Rao Vs The Secretary, Agricultural Produce Marketing Committee Balki,
Taluk
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, the disability on the whole body would have to be 12% but the PW.3 has assessed the disability on higher side.
Further when petitioner is aged about 18 years, there is every possibility of his recovering from the disabilities.
Hence, there is no reason to believe that the alleged disability would come in the way of the future earnings of the petitioner.
Hence, petitioner is not entitled for compensation under the head loss of future income.

The nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner may have caused some amount of loss of amenities and discomforts hence petitioner is entitled for compensation under the head loss of amenities and discomfort to the tune of Rs.2,00,000/-.
21. Towards pain and sufferings, petitioner shown to have sustained one grievous injury.

Hence taking in to consideration the nature of injury sustained by the petitioner and the time taken for treatment and sufferings during the treatment, it is reasonable to hold that petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.70,000/- towards pain and suffering.
22. So far as the medical expenses incurred by the petitioner is concerned, he has produced medical bills for Rs.2,09,831/- at Ex.P10/-.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the head medical expenses to the tune of Rs.2,09,831/-
23.
It is stated that petitioner was aged about 18 years and he was working with his uncle and earning sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.
But to substantiate the said contention, petitioner has not produced any materials.

Hence this court considering the age of the petitioner, the year of accident and place of residence of the petitioner takes the income of the petitioner at Rs.16,500/- p.m.
24.
The petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and has taken treatment for 6 days as inpatient in Prolife Multi Speciality Hospital, Bengaluru.

Hence the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner which is grievous in nature it is reasonable to hold that period of 4 months as complete laid down Nikhil M vs Seshadripuram Public School on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140074050/
5 period.

sentences.text: Hence taking into consideration the avocation of the petitioner and loss of income caused from the said avocation this court takes the loss of income during the laid down period as Rs.16,500/- p.m. for four months.

Hence petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.66,000/-
(Rs.16,500X4) towards loss of income during the laid down period .
25. From the evidence of Pw1 and as borne out by medical records, petitioner has taken treatment at Prolife Multi Speciality Hospital.
Further for 6 days of hospitalization requires an attendant, was traveled to hospital for treatment.
He has taken nourishment and needs further nourishment at this age and incurred other incidental expenses.
Therefore all together incidental expenses is assessed at Rs.25,000/- taking in to consideration the cost of living and value of the money during the year 2024.
26. PW.2 has stated that petitioner has to undergo one more surgery for removal of implant.
The PW.2 has not stated the estimated cost of future surgery and has not given estimation.
Hence, this court inclines to award future medical expenses to the tune of Rs.30,000/-.

The Petitioner is entitled compensation under the following heads:
Sl.No Heads Amount 1. Towards pain and sufferings Rs. 70,000/-
2. Medical expenses Rs. 2,09,831/-

3. Towards loss of income during Rs. 66,000/-
 laid up period 4.

Towards Conveyance, Attendant Rs. 25,000/-
 charges and nourishing food 5.

Future medical expenses Rs. 30,000/-
6. Loss of amenities and discomfort Rs.2,00,000/-

Therefore, this court holds that petitioner is entitled for Rs.6,00,831/- (Rupees Six Lakh Eight Hundred Thirty One only)
27.
As regarding liability is concerned, there is no dispute that offending vehicle was insured with the 2nd respondent and policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Further the driver of the offending vehicle had driving license to drive the offending vehicle.
Hence it can be said that all the documents pertaining to the vehicle in question was valid and in force as on the date of accident.

Hence by fastening liability on the respondent no.2 this court directs the respondent no.2 to pay compensation to the petitioner along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of accident till the date of payment of entire amount.
Accordingly Issue No.2 is answered.
28. Issue No.3:
In the light of findings given on Issue No.1 and 2, my finding on this issue is as per the following final order.

sentences.text: The claim petition filed by the petitioner is hereby allowed in part with costs.

The petitioner is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.6,00,831/- (Rupees Six Lakh Eight Hundred Thirty One only) with interest on Rs.5,70,831/- at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The Respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation and is directed to deposit the compensation along with interest within two months from the date of award.

On deposit of the said amount and interest, 40% of compensation payable to the petitioner shall be deposited in his name in any nationalized bank of the choice of petitioner for a period of 3 years and remaining 60% shall be released to the petitioner through E-payment on proper identification.
Advocates' fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
